classification_basis: Implemented entries were reviewed against the official page, fixtures, and both engines. Summaries, analysis classes, and delegation recommendations for unimplemented entries were drafted from the official page and assigned a status by the documented rules in docs/architecture/sei-cert-rule-pack.md; review them against the official page before promoting an entry.

rules.title: Do not store sensitive information on external storage (SD card) unless encrypted first
rules.summary: Sensitive data must not be persisted to shared external storage (SD card, OBB, mounted media) in plaintext, since other apps or people may read or alter it.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Writing secrets in cleartext to a file under the external storage directory.
rules.compliant_concept: Keep data in private internal storage, or apply sound encryption before writing externally.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags every external-storage write, including non-sensitive or already-encrypted content.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Misses writes via wrapper helpers, libraries, or paths built indirectly; cannot judge sensitivity.

rules.title: Limit the accessibility of an app's sensitive content provider
rules.summary: A content provider holding sensitive data must not be reachable by other apps; mark it non-exported or guard it with restrictive permissions, noting older API defaults.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Provider entry lacking an exported=false setting, defaulting to public on legacy API levels.
rules.compliant_concept: Provider explicitly declared non-exported, or access gated by suitable permissions.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Intentionally public providers serving nonsensitive data get flagged; permission strength not assessed.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Cannot tell which providers hold sensitive data; misses merged-manifest or targetSdk-dependent defaults.

rules.title: Do not allow WebView to access sensitive local resource through file scheme
rules.summary: A WebView rendering URIs from untrusted intents must not load file-scheme content with JavaScript enabled; validate incoming URIs and restrict file access settings.
rules.noncompliant_concept: JavaScript-enabled WebView loading an unvalidated intent-supplied URI, allowing file: scheme pages.
rules.compliant_concept: Validate received URIs, rejecting file scheme, and disable file and universal file-URL access.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags JavaScript or file-access settings even when only trusted bundled content is loaded.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Misses intent-to-loadUrl flows through helpers and validation that is present but bypassable.

rules.title: Do not broadcast sensitive information using an implicit intent
rules.summary: Intents carrying sensitive data must not be broadcast implicitly; restrict recipients via explicit target, package, permission, or in-process broadcasting.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Global sendBroadcast of an implicit intent whose extras include credentials or private data.
rules.compliant_concept: In-app local broadcast, explicit component or package, or receiver permission requirement.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Every implicit sendBroadcast matches, including harmless event notifications without sensitive extras.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Intent construction split across methods, sticky/ordered variants, or sensitivity of extras missed.

rules.title: Do not log sensitive information
rules.summary: Applications and bundled libraries must not emit sensitive information such as tokens, credentials, or location to the system log.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling android.util.Log methods with access tokens or location values.
rules.compliant_concept: Omit sensitive values from logs; gate or strip logging in release builds.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Matching all Log calls is noisy; name heuristics misjudge which variables are sensitive.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Misses logging wrappers, third-party library logging, and tainted values reaching logs indirectly.

rules.title: Do not grant URI permissions on implicit intents
rules.summary: URI read/write grant flags must not be attached to implicit intents, since an interceptor would gain access to the referenced provider data.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Setting a URI-permission grant flag on an intent with no explicit target.
rules.compliant_concept: Address the intent explicitly to the intended component before granting URI access.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: May flag intents later made explicit elsewhere, or URIs exposing nonsensitive data.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Misses flags combined via variables or intents built across methods.

rules.title: Verify the caller of intents before acting on them
rules.summary: Exported components must establish the caller's identity or require permissions before acting on received intents, especially receivers registered for system actions.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Exported receiver or service acting on intent contents without validating the sender.
rules.compliant_concept: Check caller identity or action before acting, or declare a protecting permission.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags exported components whose handlers are harmless or validate input differently.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Cannot determine whether existing identity checks are adequate or reachable on all paths.

rules.title: Protect exported services with strong permissions
rules.summary: Any exported service must be protected by a sufficiently strong permission so arbitrary apps cannot start or bind it.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Service exported (often via intent filter) without any permission requirement.
rules.compliant_concept: Service guarded by a custom signature-level or otherwise strong permission, or not exported.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Services intentionally public or protected dynamically in code would be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Weak permission protection levels or permissions defined elsewhere may not be evaluated.

rules.title: Always canonicalize a URL received by a content provider
rules.summary: File paths derived from URIs received by a content provider must be decoded and canonicalized, then confirmed to stay within the intended directory before use.
rules.noncompliant_concept: openFile building a File from getLastPathSegment output without canonical containment check.
rules.compliant_concept: Decode the path, canonicalize it, and verify it remains under the permitted base directory.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags providers already validating paths via unconventional helpers or framework utilities.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Misses traversal when URI flows through helper methods or uses alternative path APIs.

rules.title: Restrict access to sensitive activities
rules.summary: Activities meant for internal use or performing sensitive actions must not be callable by arbitrary apps; avoid exporting them or verify the caller.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Internal sensitive activity exposed by an intent filter without access restriction.
rules.compliant_concept: Activity marked non-exported, permission-protected, or verifying caller signature.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Exported launcher or deliberately public activities flagged without knowing sensitivity.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: In-code caller checks and actual sensitivity of activity behavior cannot be judged.

rules.title: Do not release apps that are debuggable
rules.summary: Release builds must not be marked debuggable in the application manifest.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Application element with debuggable attribute set to true in shipped build.
rules.compliant_concept: Debuggable left false or unset, controlled by the release build type.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Debug-only manifests or source sets may be flagged though not released.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Misses debuggable set through Gradle build types or merged manifests.

rules.title: Ensure that sensitive data is kept secure
rules.summary: Sensitive data held in files, preferences, or databases must be inaccessible to other apps, using private mode internally or private mode plus strong encryption externally.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Creating a file, preference store, or database with world-accessible mode.
rules.compliant_concept: Creating storage with private mode, encrypting when stored externally.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Mode flags flag nonsensitive files; taint heuristics overestimate sensitivity.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Leaks via intents, IPC, or other channels need taint analysis beyond syntax.

rules.title: Do not trust data from world-writable files
rules.summary: Placeholder: data read from world-writable locations should not be trusted; page lacks a defined normative condition and examples.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Not defined on page; presumably consuming data from world-writable sources.
rules.compliant_concept: Not defined on page; presumably treating such data as untrusted or avoiding it.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Without defined condition, any read from shared storage could be flagged spuriously.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Writability is a runtime property; syntax cannot establish file permissions.

rules.title: Do not provide addJavascriptInterface method access in a WebView which could contain untrusted content. (API level JELLY_BEAN or below)
rules.summary: On API 16 and below, do not expose Java objects to a WebView via addJavascriptInterface when it may load untrusted content; otherwise require minimum API 17.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Registering a JavaScript bridge object in a WebView loading untrusted content on legacy APIs.
rules.compliant_concept: Omit the bridge, or set minimum SDK to 17+ with annotated exposed methods.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags bridges when minSdk is already 17 or content is trusted.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Requires correlating minSdk from build config and content origin; syntax alone misses that.

rules.title: Check that a calling app has appropriate permissions before responding
rules.summary: When servicing another app's request using the app's own permissions, first confirm the caller holds the corresponding permission to avoid confused-deputy escalation.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Returning permission-protected results to callers without verifying their permissions.
rules.compliant_concept: Check or enforce the calling app's permission before responding.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Absence of checkCallingPermission flagged even where unnecessary or enforced in the manifest.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Cannot know which operations need caller permission checks.

rules.title: Consider privacy concerns when using Geolocation API
rules.summary: WebView geolocation permission prompts must obtain the user's explicit consent before granting websites access to device location.
rules.noncompliant_concept: onGeolocationPermissionsShowPrompt override that unconditionally grants location access.
rules.compliant_concept: Ask the user via UI and grant only on consent, honoring settings.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Overrides that grant only after a consent dialog elsewhere may be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Grant paths through callbacks or stored preferences are hard to follow syntactically.

rules.title: Explicitly define the exported attribute for private components
rules.summary: Components intended to be private should have their exported attribute set explicitly to false in the manifest rather than relying on defaults.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Private component declared without explicit exported attribute.
rules.compliant_concept: Private component with exported explicitly set to false.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Components intended to be public lacking the attribute get flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Intent of privacy unknowable syntactically; merged manifests from libraries missed.

rules.title: Do not use the Android cryptographic security provider encryption default for AES
rules.summary: Do not rely on the provider's default AES transformation, which selects ECB mode; specify a secure mode and padding explicitly.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Requesting a cipher by bare algorithm name AES, implicitly using ECB.
rules.compliant_concept: Specify an authenticated or properly IV-based mode explicitly in the transformation.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Algorithm strings for non-encryption uses, or explicitly secure ones misparsed, may be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Transformation strings built from constants or variables elsewhere evade literal matching.

rules.title: Do not use the default behavior in a cryptographic library if it does not use recommended practices
rules.summary: Avoid insecure cryptographic library defaults and common misuse such as ECB, predictable IVs, hardcoded keys or salts, weak PBE iteration counts, and fixed seeds.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Hardcoded keys, static IVs or salts, ECB mode, low PBE iterations, seeded SecureRandom.
rules.compliant_concept: Random IVs and salts, protected keys, adequate iteration counts, explicit secure modes.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Constants in tests or non-security contexts flagged as hardcoded keys or seeds.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Constant keys or IVs flowing across methods or fields escape local patterns.

rules.title: Properly verify server certificate on SSL/TLS
rules.summary: TLS clients must fully validate server certificates, including trust chain, signature, validity period, and hostname; do not install permissive trust managers or hostname verifiers.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Empty TrustManager check methods or allow-all hostname verifier enabling interception.
rules.compliant_concept: Use platform default validation, or pin/self-signed handling per established guidance.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Debug-only or test trust managers flagged; nonempty but sound custom checks may match.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Conditional enabling via flags, subtly flawed custom validation, and cleartext mixing missed.

rules.title: Specify permissions when creating files via the NDK
rules.summary: Native code creating files must explicitly set restrictive permissions or umask, since the inherited zygote umask yields world-readable and writable files.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Native file creation relying on default mode under a zero umask.
rules.compliant_concept: Set an appropriate umask or pass explicit restrictive mode to open.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Calls preceded by umask elsewhere in the process would still be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Permissive explicit modes or creation through wrappers and fopen variants missed.

rules.title: Always pass explicit intents to a PendingIntent
rules.summary: Base intents wrapped in a PendingIntent must explicitly name a component owned by the creating app; never wrap an implicit intent.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Creating a PendingIntent from an intent lacking an explicit component.
rules.compliant_concept: Set the explicit component or class on the base intent before wrapping.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Intents made explicit through methods not recognized by the pattern get flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Intents passed in from other methods or fields hide their explicitness.

rules.title: Do not cache sensitive information
rules.summary: Sensitive information must not be left in caches such as WebView caches, keyboard dictionaries, camera caches, or retained screen state.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Allowing sensitive web or UI content to persist in an accessible cache.
rules.compliant_concept: Disable or clear caching for sensitive content and inputs.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Cache-related API use flagged regardless of whether content is sensitive.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Many cache channels are implicit; absence of clearing calls is hard to detect.

rules.title: Do not use world readable or writeable to share files between apps
rules.summary: Do not share files between apps by making them world-readable or world-writable; use content providers or other formal IPC instead.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Using world-readable or world-writable mode constants for shared files or preferences.
rules.compliant_concept: Share via content provider, broadcast, or service with access control.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Low; constants could appear in unreachable legacy code or comments.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Misses permission changes via chmod, File setters, or native code.

rules.title: Do not use loopback when handling sensitive data
rules.summary: Do not transmit sensitive data over localhost sockets or bind listeners to all interfaces; use secured IPC or TLS channels.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Sending sensitive data through a loopback port or server bound to any address.
rules.compliant_concept: Use authenticated Android IPC or TLS-protected connections.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Loopback use for nonsensitive data or tests would be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Addresses built dynamically and sensitivity of traffic cannot be inferred syntactically.

rules.title: Do not bundle OAuth security-related protocol logic or sensitive data into a relying party's app
rules.summary: Placeholder: relying-party apps should not embed OAuth security logic or secrets such as client secrets; page provides no examples.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Not defined on page; presumably embedding OAuth secrets or protocol logic in the app.
rules.compliant_concept: Not defined on page; presumably delegating OAuth security handling to a server.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Secret-like strings or OAuth library usage flagged without context.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Protocol logic placement is architectural; syntax cannot assess it.

rules.title: Use constant-time encryption
rules.summary: Placeholder: cryptographic operations should execute in constant time to resist timing side channels; page has no defined content.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Not defined on page; presumably timing-variable cryptographic or comparison code.
rules.compliant_concept: Not defined on page; presumably constant-time implementations or comparisons.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Non-secret comparisons using early-exit equality would be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Timing leaks in library internals or branching on secrets are invisible syntactically.

rules.title: To request user permission for OAuth, identify relying party and its permissions scope
rules.summary: When requesting OAuth authorization, show the user the identity of the relying party and the scope of permissions requested.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Consent request omitting relying-party identity or requested scope.
rules.compliant_concept: Consent dialog naming the relying party and listing permission scope.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: UI content is not reliably recognizable as a consent prompt.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Consent dialog completeness is a UX property beyond syntax.

rules.title: For OAuth, use a secure Android method to deliver access tokens
rules.summary: OAuth access tokens must be delivered to the relying-party app through a secure Android mechanism that uniquely identifies the recipient.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Passing tokens through channels other apps can intercept or impersonate.
rules.compliant_concept: Deliver tokens via explicit intents to a recipient verified by signing key.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Token-named variables in intents flagged even when delivered explicitly.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Token identification and delivery-channel security need dataflow and design understanding.

rules.title: For OAuth, use an explicit intent method to deliver access tokens
rules.summary: OAuth access tokens must be sent only via explicit intents addressed to the specific recipient component, never implicit intents.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Placing an access token in an implicit intent.
rules.compliant_concept: Placing the token in an explicitly targeted intent.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Name-based token detection misfires on unrelated extras.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Tokens renamed or added in another method escape detection.

rules.title: Do not load world-writable libraries
rules.summary: Placeholder: apps should not load native or code libraries from world-writable locations; page has no defined content.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Not defined on page; presumably loading libraries from shared writable storage.
rules.compliant_concept: Not defined on page; presumably loading only from app-private directories.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Loads from app-private absolute paths flagged as suspicious.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Path origin and runtime writability not knowable from syntax.
